learningObjective: See that when a thin ring is cut and unrolled, it becomes a rectangle with width equal to the circumference (2πr) and height equal to the ring thickness — and that these rectangles stack into a triangular shape
ahaMoment: As rings get thinner, the stacked rectangles form a cleaner triangle shape

miniSpec.title: Making Rings Thinner
miniSpec.manipulated_variable: Reduce thickness via slider — controls how many rings divide the circle
miniSpec.primary_visual_feedback: Each strip becomes narrower as ring count increases; the stack of rectangular strips beside the circle shows more strips forming a stepped approximation to a triangle
miniSpec.goal_structure: Free exploration with implicit guidance toward increasing ring count to see cleaner triangle approximation
miniSpec.causal_chain_exposed: Circle divided into colored bands, one band with visible thickness dr, stack of rectangular strips beside circle, strips forming stepped approximation to triangle
miniSpec.trace_strategy: Current state is sufficient — focus is on the transformation at current subdivision level
miniSpec.aha_moment: As rings get thinner, the stacked rectangles form a cleaner triangle shape

modelVariables.numRings: Number of rings the circle is divided into (3-50), student-controlled via slider
modelVariables.R: Circle radius, carried over from previous section, frozen/locked at 4
modelVariables.unwrapping_dr: Derived: thickness of each ring = R / numRings
modelVariables.unwrapping_totalArea: Derived: sum of all rectangle areas, approaching πR²
modelVariables.unwrapping_outerCircumference: Derived: 2πR, width of the outermost rectangle
modelVariables.unwrapping_errorPercent: Derived: percentage error between rectangle sum and exact πR²

assertions.description: On load, the circle is divided into a small number of rings (5), showing visible stepped approximation in the triangle
assertions.visualCheck: Circle shows 5 distinct concentric colored bands; right side shows 5 rectangular strips in a stepped staircase approximating a triangle

assertions.description: The numRings slider can be operated and produces the expected visual response
assertions.visualCheck: Circle now shows 20 thinner colored bands; strips become thinner and more numerous, forming a stepped triangle shape

assertions.description: The circle radius R is carried over from section 1 and stays fixed
assertions.visualCheck: Radius R shown as fixed value (4), not interactive — carried over from slicing section

assertions.description: High ring count produces cleaner triangle approximation (the aha)
assertions.visualCheck: 50 very thin strips form a nearly smooth triangle outline; total area close to πR² ≈ 50.27

invariants.description: Ring thickness always equals R divided by number of rings
Total area of rectangles is always positive
